About MeteoOne Version %1$s · code %2$d Your location stays yours MeteoOne requests approximate location only after your action, reduces it to the 0.1° forecast grid before persistence, and never stores the raw device coordinates. Android backup is disabled. Privacy policy Offline-first The latest fused forecast and its persisted model/provider evidence remain available from the on-device cache. A failed refresh does not replace a valid cached snapshot. Weather data and attribution Forecast providers remain delivery paths grouped by model family. MeteoOne also uses public station observations for on-device verification; observation data does not become an extra forecast-model vote. Open-Meteo MeteoOne uses Open-Meteo as a forecast-data provider. Open-Meteo weather data requires attribution under CC BY 4.0. NOAA / NCEP GFS MeteoOne can retrieve GFS forecast data from NOAA/NCEP NOMADS. U.S. government NOAA/NWS information is generally public domain unless specifically noted otherwise; MeteoOne is not endorsed by or affiliated with NOAA/NWS.\n NOAA / NCEI GHCNh observations\n MeteoOne uses Global Historical Climatology Network hourly (GHCNh) public station observations for on-device forecast verification. NOAA dedicates GHCNh data to the public domain worldwide under CC0-1.0 and publishes a recommended dataset citation. ECMWF IFS Open Data This service is based on data and products of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). ECMWF Open Data is published under CC BY 4.0 and is combined with other forecast evidence by MeteoOne. ECMWF accepts no liability for errors, omissions, availability, loss, or damage arising from use of its data. DWD ICON Open Data MeteoOne can retrieve ICON forecast data from Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) Open Data. DWD Open Data terms apply CC BY 4.0. Source details Project MeteoOne is developed in a public GitHub repository. Project architecture, privacy documentation, security policy, and release controls are maintained there.
